text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — long-running inference jobs show steady RSS growth (~40MB/min) on 64k token runs. I think KV page ownership isn't getting cleared after the batch-merge path. Profiling attached.
Maria Chen: snippet from node-3 logs:
```
[14:02:01] kv: page 0x7f3a12f0 owner=None -> owner=req-42
[14:02:01] kv: page 0x7f3a12f0 append ok
[14:02:02] eviction: tried to evict page 0x7f3a12f0 -> skipped (owner tag mismatch)
[14:02:05] kv: page 0x7f3a12f0 reused with owner=req-43 but still has prev-kv refs
```
Maria Chen: repro is simple: `./tools/run_long_ctx --model small-quant --tokens 65536 --batch 4 --repeat 600` on a canary. Heap/kv memory climbs linearly.
Aj Patel: hmm. did you bisect to a commit? any recent changes to batch-merge or eviction ordering?
Maria Chen: Not a full bisect yet but perf-bot flagged a regression around the handler that changed merge ordering. See commit 9a1b2cd in the perf alert.
perf-bot: Regression alert: throughput/regression detected in commit 9a1b2cd — changed batch-merge -> eviction ordering. Suspected KV tag reuse issue.
Samir Das: I saw something similar last week — stale reads where token alignment was off by 1 after batch split. Could be the same root cause (page ownership not cleared, reused mid-request).
Lee Wong: can you paste a tiny repro that we can run in CI? I can try to repro locally on my dev GPU.
Maria Chen: posted above. also added a small instrumented run to stress eviction: `./tools/kv_stress --seq 65536 --batch 6 --stress-evict` — observed pages being marked owned but not zeroed on reclaim.
Aj Patel: quick mitigation idea: stamp a per-request epoch tag on pages at request start and verify it at reuse; if mismatch, refuse reuse and zero before reassigning. That will be a bit slower but safe.
Toni Alvarez: I'll add a unit test that does: batch-split -> merge -> force-evict -> reuse. Expectation: reused page should have owner==None before assignment.
Maria Chen: also saw alignment shifts in the KV index: offsets in the index point at token-1 sometimes, which causes the decoder to pull wrong KV slices. Might explain subtle quality regressions.
Aj Patel: can we add an assert in debug builds: `assert(page->owner == NONE || page->epoch == current_epoch)` when we attach?
Toni Alvarez: adding test + assert. Planning to push a PR that clears owner on reclaim and increments reclaim_epoch. Will run perf to measure impact.
perf-bot: Perf snapshot: baseline run RSS 6.1GB, after 9a1b2cd RSS 6.8GB at 30min.
Maria Chen: quick temporary patch applied to canary: zero owner during eviction path. Monitoring now.
ci-bot: ci-bot: rolling restart on canary group initiated (job 4421).
Lee Wong: Nice. If that stabilizes memory, we should backport an assert and the zeroing to 1st-line fix, then follow up with epoch tags for correctness.
Samir Das: note: also check KV prefetch code — it uses stale tags when prefetch and append race. Prefetch can land pages into cache with old tags.
Aj Patel: good catch. I'll audit prefetch + append ordering. Might need a tiny memory barrier or atomic tag swap.
Maria Chen: thanks team — assigning @Aj and @Toni to own the fix. I'll continue to monitor canary and post flamegraphs in this thread. :thumbsup:
Toni Alvarez: on it, will open PR with tests and CI perf run.
Aj Patel: will audit prefetch and add debug asserts.
Maria Chen: update: after quick zero-on-evict patch, canary RSS growth flattened in first 15 mins. Keeping it under observation.
Maria Chen: will post final postmortem if stable.
Lee Wong: thanks everyone.
Maria Chen: :eyes:
